questions.question_text:
Four batteries are taken from a drawer and tested.
Which event is the complement of 'at least one battery is flat'?

options.why: Exactly one is only one of the ways of getting at least one flat battery.
This can happen at the same time as at least one being flat, so it is not the complement.
Names the strongest form of the event rather than the outcomes it leaves out.

questions.solution_text:
The complement of 'at least one' is 'none'.
The complementary event is 'no battery is flat'.

questions.question_text:
Two alarm clocks are set.
The probability that neither clock rings is $\frac{1}{9}$.
What is the probability that at least one clock rings?

options.why: Repeated the given probability instead of subtracting it from $1$.
Doubled the given probability because there are two clocks, instead of subtracting from $1$.
Squared the given probability instead of subtracting it from $1$.
Found the probability that neither battery is flat but did not subtract it from $1$.
Found the probability that both batteries are flat instead of at least one.
Added the two single-battery probabilities instead of using the complement.

questions.question_text:
A netballer scores from any shot with probability $\frac{1}{4}$, and her shots are independent.
She takes three shots.
What is the probability that she scores at least one goal?

options.why: Found the probability of scoring no goals but did not subtract it from $1$.
Found the probability of scoring from all three shots instead of at least one.
Multiplied $\frac{1}{4}$ by $3$, treating 'at least one' as three separate chances.
Found the probability that neither battery is flat but did not subtract it from $1$.
Treated the draws as with replacement, keeping both the working count and total unchanged: $1-\frac{5}{9}\times\frac{5}{9}=\frac{56}{81}$.
Found the probability that both batteries are flat instead of at least one.

questions.question_text:
A string of fairy lights lights up only when all four of its globes work.
The probability that all four globes work is $0.88$.
What is the probability that at least one globe does not work?

options.why: Repeated the probability that all four globes work instead of subtracting it from $1$.
Divided $0.88$ by $4$ to get 'one globe' rather than using the complement.
Divided the complement by $4$, as if the chance were shared equally between the globes.

questions.solution_text:
The complement of 'at least one does not work' is 'all four work'.
$P(\text{at least one does not work}) = 1 - 0.88$
$= 0.12$

The complement of 'at least one rings' is 'neither rings'.
$P(\text{neither rings}) = 0.2 \times 0.2$
$= 0.04$

$= 0.96$

questions.question_text:
A box contains $13$ light globes, $5$ of which are faulty.
Three globes are taken out one after the other without replacement.
What is the probability that at least one globe is faulty?

options.why: Found the probability that no globe is faulty but did not subtract it from $1$.
Gave the probability that the first globe is faulty instead of using all three draws.
Found the probability that all three globes are faulty: $\frac{5}{13}\times\frac{4}{12}\times\frac{3}{11}=\frac{5}{143}$.

questions.question_text: What is the probability that I win at least one game? [tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.75]\draw (0,0)--(2,1) node[midway,above] {$0.6$} node[right] {Win};\draw (0,0)--(2,-1) node[midway,below] {$0.4$} node[right] {Lose};\draw (2,1)--(4,1.8) node[midway,above] {$0.6$} node[right] {Win};\draw (2,1)--(4,0.2) node[midway,below] {$0.4$} node[right] {Lose};\draw (2,-1)--(4,-0.2) node[midway,above] {$0.6$} node[right] {Win};\draw (2,-1)--(4,-1.8) node[midway,below] {$0.4$} node[right] {Lose};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]

options.why: Counted only the win-then-lose path, $0.6\times0.4=0.24$, omitting the other paths with a win.
Counted exactly one win, $0.6\times0.4+0.4\times0.6=0.48$, omitting winning both games.
Found the probability of winning both games, $0.6\times0.6=0.36$, instead of at least one.

questions.solution_text: The only way not to win at least one game is to lose both games, with probability $0.4\times0.4=0.16$. Therefore $P(\text{at least one win})=1-0.16=0.84$.
